At the office365 call site the parsed data is spread over o365AuthCredentials and persisted, so if refreshTokenResponseSchema omits/strips refresh_token (cannot be fully verified from the diff), the real refresh token is replaced by the literal placeholder and saved, breaking the credential. The unguarded mutation is clearly visible in the diff; only the schema-dependent impact is uncertain.

judged_text: The refresh_token: 'refresh_token' placeholder mutation is not gated on sync mode, so it also fires during normal (non-sync) operation whenever the app's token schema does not surface refresh_token in the parsed data. At the office365 call site the parsed data is spread over o365AuthCredentials, so whenever refreshTokenResponseSchema strips or the provider omits refresh_token, the real refresh token is overwritten with the literal string 'refresh_token' and persisted, permanently breaking that credential's refresh until the user re-authenticates.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the code unconditionally mutates `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` to the literal string `"refresh_token"` whenever it is missing (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { ... }`), regardless of whether sync mode is enabled. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the parsed token data is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`) and then persisted. If the provider omits `refresh_token` on refresh (common) or the schema doesn’t surface it, this placeholder will overwrite the previously valid `refresh_token` and be saved, breaking future refreshes until re-auth.
